# fastf 3.0.0 — the guided app on ratatui

The guided menu — a sequence of prompts, one question at a time — is gone. `fastf` opens one full-screen dashboard over the whole library: every base, every template, folder sizes filling in as they are measured, fuzzy search with the `fastf search` grammar, a command palette that finds any command or project by name, and every verb a key away. Every flow that builds something is a form, then a preview built by the code that commits it, then Enter. Templates get a studio with a builder that draws the folder tree beside the paths as you type them. Every setting is on one screen with its value beside it. The command line's own prompts — the ambiguity picker, a confirmation, a text field — are drawn by the same ratatui, a few rows at the cursor, and `dialoguer` is gone.

## What the app does now

- **Marks make a verb a batch.** Space marks a row; `*` marks the view; every verb but rename then runs over all of them, asking its one question once — a tag, the tags to remove, a note, the base to move to, the word `delete`. One item at a time, each row patched as its item lands, a report that leaves the unrun rows marked.
- **Delete asks for the word `delete`**, names the folder (or the folders), and a typo keeps your text.
- **One registry.** Every key, palette entry, help line and key line comes from one list — including the studio's, the builder's and the settings'. `?` (or F1) opens the help for wherever you are, inside any dialog. In the action menu a verb's own key runs it.
- **A quick note takes several lines** (Enter saves, Alt-Enter breaks a line), and a paste can never become keystrokes: a single-line field keeps the first line and says so, the dashboard ignores a paste and says so, and a paste a terminal delivers as keystrokes is recognised as one.
- **A message log.** `L` reads back every status line and warning of the session, newest first, with the time it arrived; a warning that flashed under a dialog is counted until you read it.
- **Session memory.** The sort order, the detail pane and the row you were on survive a restart (`state.toml` beside `config.toml`).
- **The look.** Columns measured from their content, so nothing runs into anything; the header counts the templates on disk and the strip lists orphan slugs dimmed after them; the split favours the table so long folder names keep their size column; an empty table says so inside the box; the help ends with the version and where the data lives.
- **A bare terminal is told the truth.** `theme = auto|mono|ansi|rich` (and `FASTF_THEME`) for terminals that announce nothing — an ssh session forwards no `COLORTERM`; truecolor is recognised from `TERM`/`TERM_PROGRAM` too; `FASTF_ASCII=0` keeps Unicode in the legacy Windows console. Without a display `o` and `t` say so instead of pretending. Ctrl-Z suspends. A second `kill -INT`, SIGHUP or a panic always give the terminal back. `fastf 2>/dev/null` repeats its refusal on stdout. The idle app wakes twice a second, not twenty-two times.
- **Register** takes a typed date, as `--created` does.

## On the command line

- `fastf rename`, `fastf unregister`, `fastf delete` — the action menu's verbs, with the app's own questions and `--yes` for scripts. Nothing the app does is app-only any more.
- `fastf config set theme …`, and `preview-lines` is documented.
- Search stopped guessing at two kinds of word: a number means an ID, and a word containing `/` is a literal tag path.

## Breaking

- `show-banner` and `show-frame` are gone with the menu they drew. `fastf config set` still accepts them and says they are ignored; a `config.toml` that names them still parses.
- `recent-default-limit` is now `recent-limit`. The old key still parses.
- The Windows legacy console (conhost) gets an ASCII alphabet automatically; every emulator that announces itself — Windows Terminal, Alacritty, WezTerm, ConEmu, VS Code — keeps Unicode. `FASTF_ASCII=1`/`0` forces either.

## Requirements

A terminal of at least 60×16; the detail pane from 100 columns, the template strip from 30 rows. Linux, Windows (MSI or zip); macOS from source.
